AttributeDef.description:
One attribute tile agents may set. The super defines these; we compile them to JSON Schema.

This *is* the restricted meta-schema: the super can't emit arbitrary JSON Schema, only
typed, bounded attributes, so the compiled schema is always valid for strict structured
output and for jsonschema validation.

enum_values.description: Allowed values for enum / enum_list types; empty otherwise.

minimum.description: Lower bound for integer/number; null otherwise.

maximum.description: Upper bound for integer/number; null otherwise.

AttributeDef.title: AttributeDef

BuildingsSpec.description:
Buildings as terrain: the engine lays out footprints on the world pixel grid, raises each
building FLOOR_LEVELS relief levels per floor (in 3D they are real blocks with pixel-art facades),
paints roofs into the ground and leaves the gaps (streets, alleys, yards) in the material's own
pattern. Use it for any built terrain: city blocks, row houses, villages, towers, castles, ports.

layout.description: blocks: staggered city blocks with alleys. rows: terraced/row houses side by side (Victorian streets, old towns). detached: houses with yards (suburbs, villages). towers: few large towers with plazas between (downtowns). compound: one big walled building per lot with a courtyard (castles, cloisters, warehouses).

lot_px.description: Typical footprint size in pixels (6-40; a tile is ~55px).

gap_px.description: Alley/yard width between buildings in pixels (1-8).

street_grid.description: City streets on the world's shared street lattice, so they join up across tiles and districts: 0 = no street grid (villages, castles, estates), 1 = a street on every lattice line (dense blocks about half a tile wide), 2 = every other line (big blocks, a tile wide).

street_material.description: The world's street connector name (e.g. 'street') that the grid streets are paved with, so they look exactly like the connector streets; '' = plain asphalt.

coverage.description: Share of lots that hold a building (0.2-1).

tall_share.description: Share of buildings near floors_max (the skyline); the rest skew low.

facade.description: Window pattern drawn on the walls: punched (brick/plaster, a grid of windows), glass (curtain-wall towers), bands (office ribbon windows), victorian (tall narrow bays), industrial (sparse high windows), stone (castles, few slits).

lit.description: Share of lit (warm) windows, 0-1 (night cities high).

roof.description: flat, parapet (raised rim), gabled (a ridge), terrace (stepped).

BuildingsSpec.title: BuildingsSpec

CopySpec.description:
Lets the super reuse a tile instead of generating a new one (cheap filler: open sea, plain
desert...). The source must be a non-copy tile in this plan or an accepted tile in the world.

- shallow: a linked instance. The copy shares the prototype's art and data, and stays in sync if
  the prototype changes later.
- deep: an independent snapshot. The copy gets its own record at copy time and never changes
  when the prototype does. `copy_of` is kept only as provenance.

source_q.description: Prototype tile q (ignored when mode is 'none').

source_r.description: Prototype tile r (ignored when mode is 'none').

CopySpec.title: CopySpec

Directive.description: What the super asks of one tile agent (derived from a PlannedTile, plus retry feedback).
Directive.title: Directive

edge.description: Edge index 0..5 (0 E, 1 NE, 2 NW, 3 W, 4 SW, 5 SE).

terrain.description: Terrain along this edge; one of the world's terrain_vocabulary.

connectors.description: Connectors crossing this edge (subset of connector_vocabulary).

HeightOp.description:
Relief pattern, evaluated per BLOCK in world space: selected blocks are raised/lowered by
`delta` levels (one level = one pixel-cube high). 'lots' raises building lots (city blocks, with
varied heights); 'rooms' raises the walls of a room grid (interiors), leaving doorways.

scale.description: Feature size in pixels (8-48 for block-scale relief).

HeightOp.title: HeightOp

rank.description: 0-9 height rank; higher materials get a dark lip where they meet lower ones.

boundary.description: How this material's own border pixels look: foam (water), glow (lava), lip, none.

block_style.description: How each 8px block is drawn: 'bevel' (lit top-left, shaded bottom-right; stone, dirt, grass, obsidian), 'outline' (dark 1px frame: bricks, planks, tiles), 'flat' (liquids, snow, sand).

edges.description: 'straight' for built things: streets, canals, corridors and walls run in straight lines between tile edges; 'organic' (rivers, trails, coasts) meanders.

markings.description: Connectors only: 'dashed' paints a road's dashed centre line and kerbs (streets, highways), 'rails' two rails with sleepers (railways, tram and cable-car lines), 'none' otherwise.

height.description: Base relief level 0-4 (liquids 0, plains 1, hills 2, rock 3+).

elevation.description: Large-scale rise in relief levels (0-40), grown by the engine as a smooth, ridged landform that blends into neighbouring terrains: 0 flat land and water, 2-5 rolling hills, 6-14 foothills and rocky slopes, 15-40 mountains and snow peaks (a level is ~1/18 of a tile's width). Cities on hills can use it too.

scatter.description: Ambient sprites for tiles of this material (<= 2 kinds).

buildings.description: For BUILT terrain only: buildings raised out of this ground as 3D blocks. The material's own colours and ops then describe the streets/yards between them.

ParentLink.description: A drilled layer: this world is the inside of one tile of its parent world.
ParentLink.title: ParentLink

PatternOp.description:
One layer of a material, evaluated in world pixel coordinates (seamless across tiles).

patches:  smooth noise blobs, coverage = amount       stripes: waves at `angle`, period = scale
speckle:  random single pixels, density = amount      cells:   voronoi cracks/mortar, width ~ amount
cellfill: fill a fraction (amount) of voronoi cells    bevel:   per-cell light/dark bevel (stones)
decals:   stamp `pixels` on a jittered grid (cell = scale, density = amount)
built environments (cities, interiors):
lots:     rectangular building lots on a staggered grid with 2px alleys, lot size = scale,
          share of lots filled = amount (each lot varies its shade: rooftops, market stalls)
rooms:    wall lines of a room grid (room size = scale) with doorways (door chance = amount)
checker:  checkerboard floor tiles (tile size = scale)
planks:   wooden floorboards (board length = scale), dark seams
bricks:   brick/stone courses (brick length = scale), mortar lines
PatternOp.title: PatternOp

leave_empty.description: True to deliberately leave this slot empty.

intent.description: One sentence: what this tile is and its role in the world.

edge_hints.description: Edge constraints the super wants (may be partial).

duplicate.description: Copy another tile instead of generating (mode 'none' to generate).

PropSpec.description: A sprite standing on the tile (tree, castle, campfire...). Rendered as its own layer.

kind.description: What it is, e.g. 'castle', 'pine tree', 'campfire', 'dark obelisk'.

PropSpec.title: PropSpec

max_tiles.description: Upper bound on tiles the super may plan (it picks the shape).

radius.description: Deprecated: a hexagon of this radius' worth of tiles.

tile_px.description: Ground texture resolution per tile (32-128px). Only for a new world: all tiles of a world share one pixel grid, so extensions keep the world's resolution.

region_radius.description: Only for a new world: radius of the region grid you find when entering a tile (then locked).

fill_radius.description: Plan every tile within the world radius (drilled layers fill their hex).

kind.description: Sprite kind placed around this material, e.g. 'oak tree', 'boulder'.

count.description: Sprites per tile of this material (0-8).

chance.description: Share of this material's tiles that get it (0-1).

Scene.description: A tile seen up close: a layered, animated pixel-art picture of the spot.
Scene.title: Scene

style.description: 1-5 consistency with the style guide and anchor tile

edge_continuity.description: 1-5 how well edges continue into accepted neighbors

directive_fit.description: 1-5 how well it matches its directive

ShapeOp.description:
One primitive on the sprite canvas (pixel units, origin top-left).

rect: top-left (x, y), size (w, h) | ellipse: center (x, y), radii (w, h)
tri: apex (x, y), base at y+h, half-width w | line: (x, y) -> (x+w, y+h) | pixel: (x, y)

frames.description: Frames this shape appears in; [] = every frame.

ShapeOp.title: ShapeOp

SkirtTile.description:
Ground just outside a region, continuing its rim terrain so the region blends into its
surroundings (rendered by the engine alone, never planned or reviewed).
SkirtTile.title: SkirtTile

width.description: Canvas width in pixels (4-18). Match the ground's pixel scale.

colors.description: 1-6 base colors '#rrggbb'; each gets a ramp (dark/base/light/hi).

shapes.description: Painted in order (later shapes on top). <= 80.

motion.description: Procedural motion applied by the renderer.

StyleGuide.description: Shared visual contract for every tile in a world. Set once, then reused.

palette.description: Master palette, 12-32 '#rrggbb' colors. Every tile pixel maps to one.

tile_px.description: Tile ground resolution in pixels (set by the engine from the run options).

outline.description: Outline rule, e.g. 'no outlines' or '1px dark outline on props'.

style_keywords.description: Short art-direction keywords appended to every image prompt.

StyleGuide.title: StyleGuide

TileLayer.description:
One visual layer of a tile. The ground layer is the seamless top-face texture. Sprite layers
stand on it as upright billboards: side-view pixel art, optionally a horizontal strip of animation
frames, plus a procedural motion the renderer applies.
TileLayer.title: TileLayer

label.description: The number drawn on the candidate in the composite image.

feedback.description: If rejected: concrete, actionable fix for the tile agent. Else ''.

sprite_feedback.description: If the landmark sprite itself needs work: an instruction for the sprite artist. Else ''.

material_feedback.description: If a terrain's shared ground pattern looks wrong: '<material name>: instruction' for the material artist (repaints every tile using it). Else ''.

region_radius.description: Radius of the region grid inside each tile (set at creation).

terrain_vocabulary.description: Allowed edge/biome terrain names (snake_case), e.g. grass, water, sand, rock, snow.

connector_vocabulary.description: Allowed linear features that cross tile edges (snake_case), e.g. road, river, wall.

directional_notes.description: General layout direction, e.g. 'mountains north, coast east'.

prop_scale.description: Size of every sprite relative to the tile, world-wide (0.3-1.5): 1 when a tile is a landscape chunk or a room, ~0.5 when a tile is a city block (people and cars next to real buildings), up to 1.3 for close-up interiors or board-game spaces.
